relation.description: Public linear-matrix-family approximation uses exact two-sided matvec queries and Frobenius error; the present task uses tolerance-priced scalar measurements and uniform function reconstruction.
Both use exact one-point adversarial values, but this class includes smoothness, strong convexity, and a conditioned family of known convex bodies.
Both study unknown nonstochastic linear control, but the disturbance-response comparator and Markov-tail model differ from known-stabilizer, strongly controllable fixed-feedback contracts.
The reward and objective structure coincide at two objectives, but no upper bound for the local tradeoff is supplied.
The unknown-envelope class removes public tradeoff information; its anchor-plus-tie regimes retain the same Lipschitz reward structure.
Action-point gradient feedback is shared, but the feasible set here is hidden behind charged separation queries rather than a known ball with free projection.

relation.notes: Immediate selected-arm feedback is a different protocol. The delay and the cap on outstanding feedback change which information becomes available.

relation.description: The existing two-radius profile assumes Euclidean gradient smoothness. This profile imposes ell-p-to-dual-ell-p smoothness and retains the two independent radii of one common minimizer.

The fixed narrow-cube profile ties the feasible circumradius to R. Here the product domain and the nearby-optimizer radius are independent, and the complexity takes a worst case over public product geometries.

The local function assumptions and known-spectrum communication are related, but the present class allows unrestricted local work and stopping-time expected sample cost rather than a fixed joint budget under the historical-vector protocol.
The resolvent setting permits an arbitrary positive Euclidean step size and measures an operator residual; the present coefficient and non-Euclidean power are fixed and the target is objective error.
The neighboring profile also hides smoothness and gap budgets. Here L and Delta are public, while p and sigma remain hidden.
The neighboring rich-jet oracle bundles values and gradients with a Hessian; this derivative-only interface does not.
The weighted derivative-only profile lacks the separate L1 promise and optimizes a priced sum instead of strict joint caps.
The information packets agree, but this model adds a gradient-Lipschitz bound and a public weighted cost.
The neighboring strict-cap derivative-only problem does not bundle gradients with Hessians.
The existing profile requires globally convex Lipschitz components and allows full-space queries. This contract requires only ball-domain functions and permits only ball-domain queries.
The p=infinity, order-three norm agrees with the operator endpoint, while the present class omits a global gradient-smoothness upper bound and fixes Gaussian noise.
